Let  
\[
f(x)=\frac{x+1}{5-3x}.
\]
Then \(x_{i+1}=f(x_i)\), and \(x_1=x_{43}\) means
\[
f^{42}(x_1)=x_1.
\]

The fixed points satisfy
\[
x=\frac{x+1}{5-3x}
\]
so
\[
x(5-3x)=x+1 \implies 3x^2-4x+1=0 \implies x=1 \text{ or } x=\frac13.
\]

To see these are the only real periodic points, set
\[
w=\frac{x-1}{x-\frac13}.
\]
Then
\[
w_{i+1}=\frac{f(x_i)-1}{f(x_i)-\frac13}=2w_i.
\]
Thus \(w_{43}=2^{42}w_1\). Since \(x_1=x_{43}\), we need \(w_{43}=w_1\), so
\[
2^{42}w_1=w_1 \implies w_1=0 \text{ or } w_1=\infty.
\]
These correspond to \(x_1=1\) or \(x_1=\frac13\), giving constant sequences.

Therefore the possible sums are
\[
42\cdot 1=42
\]
and
\[
42\cdot \frac13=14.
\]
Their product is
\[
42\cdot 14=588.
\]

\[
\boxed{588}
\]
